# Orazaka

> Orazaka is an open-source AI platform by Krizaka (Montréal): chat, documents, images, video and agents running on your own machines, with local models. A product of Krizaka (Montréal), open source under Apache-2.0. Sign-in is closed on this development site.

## Key pages

- [Home](https://www.orazaka.com/): what Orazaka is
- [Absolute privacy](https://www.orazaka.com/features/absolute-privacy): Every model, every file and every conversation stays on machines you control. Orazaka does not phone home — there is nothing to opt out of.
- [One engine](https://www.orazaka.com/features/unified-engine): Chat, documents, images, video, speech and agents share one runtime, one identity and one bill. One pipeline governs every request, whatever it asks for.
- [Agents with consent](https://www.orazaka.com/features/infinite-reach): The Orazaka agent runs on your machine and connects out to your workspace. It does real work — files, scripts, your tools — and every action waits for a human approval.
- [Mobile app](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/mobile): recordings and screenshots of the iOS and Android app
- [Orazaka for Mac](https://www.orazaka.com/desktop): the Orazaka Desktop test build for Apple Silicon — what it does today, requirements, download
- [Gallery](https://www.orazaka.com/gallery): images made with Orazaka
- [Models](https://www.orazaka.com/models): the 30 models Orazaka supports — what each does, where it runs, its licence and context window
- [Talk to the team](https://www.krizaka.com/contact?topic=orazaka): the contact form lives on krizaka.com

## Documentation

- [Documentation hub](https://www.orazaka.com/docs): architecture, packs and Studios, the API, administration, the CLI
- [Orazaka in ten minutes](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/101): What Orazaka is, how it is put together, and your first chat, image and Studio run from a fresh checkout.
- [Install, update & back up](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/self-hosting): Requirements, the three-step installs for a Mac and for a Linux server, then living with it: health, updates, rollback, backups and removal. Your data never leaves your machine.
- [Glossary](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/glossary): The words used across these docs, in plain language.
- [Packs & Studios](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/packs): The packs that extend Orazaka without code: the reference catalogue, each manifest field, and how to write, validate and install a pack.
- [Playbook: build a product on Orazaka](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/business-playbook): A worked example — what to deploy, in what order, and what each step delivers — written for decision-makers as much as engineers.
- [Jobs, schedules & automation](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/jobs): Everything Orazaka runs without a person waiting: the job plane, its workers, every scheduled task and the automation connectors.
- [Supported models](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/models): Every model Orazaka supports: where it runs, its licence and its context window, read from the registry the routing reads.
- [Measured runs](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/measured-runs): Time, cost and every parameter of the video and image runs Orazaka made — per model and provider, read from the run records, with the failures and their causes.
- [Cinematic shorts](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/cinematic-shorts): A 30–60 s film from a brief — directed shot list, character references, Wan 2.2 A14B shots, an upscaled cut with ramps, grade and titles, music, foley and voice — each step an ordinary Studio run, gated frame by frame.
- [Content policy — you decide](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/content-policy): What Orazaka refuses by itself, what the operator of an installation decides, and how a run is checked before a GPU second is spent.
- [Administration](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/admin): What an administrator controls — models, the interceptor pipeline, capabilities, plans, wallets, Studios — and how the console is secured.
- [Authentication & sessions](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/auth): How identity, sessions and access control work, flow by flow.
- [Security policy](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/security): How to report a vulnerability, which versions get fixes, and what a self-hosted installation provides.
- [Licensing](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/licensing): What the Apache-2.0 licence covers across the Orazaka repositories, and where the proprietary line falls.
- [API reference](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/api): Every REST endpoint of every service, with the authorisation rule that guards it.
- [CLI reference](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/cli): One tool for the whole platform: every command, subcommand and option of the orazaka CLI.
- [Tools & MCP](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/tools): What a model may call during a turn: registered tools, the MCP servers, the tool cache and the write sandbox.
- [Worker protocol](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/worker-protocol): The AMQP contract a worker speaks to join the platform — bindings, envelopes, progress and failure — in any language.
- [Automation & the local agent](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/automation): The protocol of the local executing agent and the automation worker.
- [Interface contracts](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/interface-contracts): Inbound and outbound ports per module, extracted from the code.
- [Architecture reference](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/architecture): The module map, dependencies, runtime flows, interceptor pipeline and messaging topology, read from the code.
- [The core engine & its pipeline](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/core): The stateless orchestration core and the request pipeline every interaction flows through.
- [Interceptor registry](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/interceptors): Every cross-cutting interceptor of the pipeline and its database-driven order.
- [The business layer](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/business): Where a request becomes business: intentions, use-cases, the dispatcher and the ports to the engine.
- [Use-case catalogue](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/use-cases): The App Factory use-cases of the business layer.
- [Repositories](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/repositories): One GitHub repository per component, what each holds and what it depends on.
- [Governance rules](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/governance): The architecture rules the build enforces, and the test suites behind each.
- [Decision records](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/adrs): The Architecture Decision Records cited across the code, and the rationale behind the structure.
- [The mobile app in four steps](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/mobile): Sign in, run a Studio, ask the model, follow your jobs — four screens, each explained.
- [The mobile app, screen by screen](https://www.orazaka.com/docs/mobile-guide): What the iOS and Android app does today, how to run it against the local stack, its tests, and which screens do not read the server yet.
- Full text of the documentation: https://www.orazaka.com/llms-full.txt
